result.finding: Assessed 5 CWE rules in Credentials & Secrets: 2 FOUND, 3 NOT_FOUND
evidence: Reviewed application authentication, runtime profiles, compose, Oracle initialization, Azure setup/reset and environment template. Runtime passwords are externalized and setup passwords generated with cryptographic RNG; no active hardcoded password/key confirmed. Reports contain no secret literals. Host-specific ACLs and external audit systems not validated.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Password
values.description: The product contains a hard-coded password, which it uses for its own inbound authentication or for outbound communication to external components.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Cryptographic Key
values.description: The product uses a hard-coded, unchangeable cryptographic key.

values.name: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

evidence.explanation: azure-setup.ps1 stores the generated database password ([MASKED]) in the project .env via Out-File (299), without setting a restrictive Unix mode/umask or Windows ACL before or after creation. On a shared Unix host with the common 022 umask, a newly created file is readable by other local users, exposing application database credentials. This is a conditional deployment-script permission finding, not a claim that the current host has executed the script or that an existing .env currently has weak permissions. Git ignore does not restrict local file access.

values.description: The product specifies permissions for a security-critical resource in a way that allows that resource to be read or modified by unintended actors.

values.name: Insufficient Logging

evidence.explanation: The authenticated destructive DetailController.deletePhoto action logs the target photo ID and outcome (69), and PhotoServiceImpl.deletePhoto similarly logs only the target ID (212). Neither records the acting authenticated principal, source or an audit correlation identity. Consequently these security-critical mutation records do not identify the actor. SecurityConfig uses HTTP Basic without an application audit handler; external proxy/SIEM audit coverage is unknown. Operational logging exists, but relevant audit details are omitted.

values.description: When a security-critical event occurs, the product either does not record the event or omits important details about the event when logging it.

values.name: Use of Hard-coded Credentials
values.description: The product contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password or cryptographic key.
